title: PPTX to JPG – Turn PowerPoint Slides into Images Free
description: Turn each PowerPoint slide into a JPG image in your browser, about 2000 px wide for a 16:9 slide, several in one ZIP. Free, and nothing is uploaded.
heading: PowerPoint to JPG
subtitle: Turn every slide of a PowerPoint file into a sharp JPG picture, several at once in a ZIP; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Convert PPTX to JPG online without PowerPoint: each slide is drawn the way this site's PowerPoint viewer (beta) shows it and saved as a JPG picture at 200 dpi, about 2000 px wide for a 16:9 slide. One slide gives one .jpg; a whole deck gives a ZIP with the slides numbered in order. Handy for posting a slide on social media, adding it to a document or sending it to a phone. Works with .pptx, .ppsx, .potx and .pptm files. Your file never leaves your device.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your file is handled by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees it.

features.title: Sharp pictures

features.title: Numbered in order

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your file is read and changed by your own browser, on your device, and is never sent anywhere. You can check it: open your browser's network panel while you use the tool and you will see no upload.

faq.question: How do I save a PowerPoint slide as a JPG without PowerPoint?
faq.answer: Keynote on a Mac, LibreOffice Impress and Google Slides can all export slides as pictures for free. In OpenAnyDoc, choose the .pptx file and download a JPG of every slide, numbered in a ZIP; it is converted in your browser and never uploaded.

faq.question: How large are the pictures?
faq.answer: Each slide is drawn at 200 dpi: about 2000 px wide for a 16:9 slide. To make the files smaller, run them through Compress image.

faq.question: Can I choose which slides to save?
faq.answer: No: every slide is saved, as a JPG at 200 dpi, with no size or format choice. Keep the JPGs you need from the ZIP.

faq.question: Will it look exactly like PowerPoint?
faq.answer: Close, not identical: the slides follow this site's PowerPoint viewer, which is in beta, and fonts your browser doesn't have are replaced. Open the file in the PowerPoint viewer to see how it will come out.

faq.question: Can I get a PDF instead?
faq.answer: Yes. PowerPoint to PDF saves one page per slide, with text you can search.

faq.question: Is it really free?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no account, no watermark and no limit on how often you use it.
